notes.title: "BBQ Grills", Tutorial, Shilka Rebalance and much more!
notes.notes:
[p]Greetings, pilots![/p][p]I continue to improve the game and sincerely thank everyone for both positive and negative feedback - it helps make the game better! [/p][p][/p][p]This is a major update that adds many new features and improvements:[/p][p]🎯 Rebalance "Shilka"
I took your feedback into account. The Shilka is now less accurate. Additionally, you can adjust its accuracy yourself for a more challenging gameplay![/p][p]⚙️ Rate Settings
You asked for it - I made it! Now you can customize rates in the game to your liking, just like with real drones.[/p][p]🌬️ Wind Volume Adjustment
A small feature requested by the community on Discord. You can now adjust wind volume through the overall weather volume setting.[/p][p]🛩️ Customizable Balance, Drone Physics, and Target Parameters
Finally, I finished what I’ve been promising for a while - now everyone can tweak individual balance parameters if needed! Before starting a mission, you can adjust drone and target settings to tailor the gameplay to yourself. I’ll add more parameters later, so if you feel something’s missing, send your suggestions! You can reduce drone weight or make enemy vehicles slower — everyone can build their own gameplay. Maybe it’s time to start planning a mission editor? Let me know if you’re interested![/p][p]🛡️ Cumulative Screens “BBQ Grills” Drones have changed the rules of modern warfare and forced the enemy to adapt. A new system of additional vehicle protection has been added - cumulative screens, so-called “mangals,” which reduce damage from drone attacks. Pilots will need to plan their attacks better and use explosive warheads to break these “mangals” on enemy vehicles![/p][p]🎓 Drone Control Tutorial
The first version of the training has been created, focusing on maintaining altitude, flying forward and sideways, making turns, and exercising full control. This should help newcomers learn the art of piloting and take to the skies! I plan to improve the tutorial based on your feedback.[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you for your support and feedback - it helps make the game better![/p][p][/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="5FLHePi3qe4;full"][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Aerodynamics and Hit Registration Update
notes.notes:
Greetings, pilots!

A new update is now available — it brings a series of technical and gameplay improvements, and sets the stage for a major upcoming update. 

Here's what's been added:

🎥 Camera Angle and FOV
When adjusted, the camera angle and field of view (FOV) are displayed in the interface. You can also set default values for both parameters in the settings.

💨 Propwash Effect
A basic simulation of the propwash effect has been added — flights now feel a bit more realistic.

🎯 Improved Hit Registration System
The accuracy of hit detection on vehicles and objects has been significantly improved.

💥 Shaped Charge Jet Mechanics
Vehicle damage now depends on the direction of the explosion. The damage may be significantly reduced if the shaped charge is not aimed directly at the target. Choosing the right attack angle is key to maximizing damage.

🛠️ Bug Fixes and Stability Improvements
Many issues have been fixed to improve game stability.

🔧 What's Next?
I’m already working on a major update that will introduce electronic warfare (EW) systems and dynamic vehicle armor (grill cages). It's coming soon — stay tuned!

Thank you to everyone helping to make this project better!

notes.title: Experimental support for TBS and DJI FPV controllers
notes.notes:
Greetings, pilots!

A new update is now live! Thank you all for your activity and bug reports — here’s what this update brings:

🎮 Experimental support for TBS and DJI FPV controllers
This is the first step toward supporting TBS and DJI FPV controllers. The functionality is currently in testing. If you're using these controllers, please share your experience in the community.
❗️Note: DJI RC, DJI RC-N1 (N2, N3) are not supported yet — only DJI FPV for now.

⚙️ Dead zones for sticks
You can now configure stick dead zones to avoid accidental drone movement caused by slight deviations in the stick position.

🐞 Controller bug fixes
Fixed an issue where, with a factory control profile selected, menu button animations would appear when pressing a button on a connected controller, but the input itself wouldn’t register. If you’re still experiencing this issue, please report it in the community and include your controller model.

🏭 "Factory" map
Fixed issues with radio interference not functioning properly on this map.

🎯 Weak points and hit registration
Improved hit detection on vehicle weak points, especially at high drone speeds. Hits should now register more reliably.

❗️If you're having issues with the new version, please report them and switch to the previous stable version. In Steam, right-click the game in your Library → "Properties" → "Betas" → choose "previous_version". To return to the latest version, select "None".

Thanks for sticking with me — more exciting updates are on the way! 🚀

notes.title: Armor and Weak Zones
notes.notes:
Greetings, pilots! Today, I’ll tell you about one of the game’s key mechanics — the system of vehicle weak points. In Remote Reaper: FPV Drone, every target has its vulnerabilities.

🔹 Armor and Weak Zones
Military vehicles are not destroyed with a single hit — they are protected by armor. However, each machine has weak points: lightly armored areas, fuel tanks, joints, or external equipment. Hitting these spots deals critical damage, allowing you to destroy a target with minimal effort.

🔹 Planning
Before attacking, a pilot should study the target’s structure on the training map and determine the right attack angle. Random hits on armor can lead to wasted ammunition and lost drones, whereas a precise shot to a weak point eliminates the target instantly.

🔹 What’s Next?
In the future, I plan to add protective structures, such as mesh screens, which are often used in real life to defend against FPV drones. You’ll need to bypass this protection just like the target’s armor.

This mechanic makes each battle more dynamic and realistic, bringing gameplay closer to real-world FPV drone tactics.

How do you like this system? Leave your comments and share your ideas — your feedback helps me improve the game! 🚀

notes.title: Drone control
notes.notes:
Greetings, pilots! 
Today, I’ll tell you about a key gameplay mechanic — drone control. Unlike other simulators, this game offers not only standard controls but also a simplified option that doesn’t require piloting skills or a controller.

🔹 Standard Controller Controls
Remote Reaper: FPV Drone was initially developed with controller support to provide a realistic drone piloting experience.

🔸Did you find it inconvenient to reach for the keyboard every time to respawn? I listened to your feedback and added a controller switch respawn feature. Now, if your drone gets shot down, you can instantly respawn it by simply flipping a switch.

🔹 Simplified Keyboard and Mouse Controls
Not everyone has a controller or knows how to fly, so I also implemented an alternative keyboard and mouse control scheme. It’s intuitive and beginner-friendly. The keys control horizontal movement, while the camera and rotation are managed with the mouse. The spacebar allows you to gain altitude, and the Shift key boosts your drone’s speed.

With these two control options, every player can choose the most comfortable way to pilot and enjoy the game.

Which control scheme do you prefer? Your feedback helps me make the game even better. 🚀

notes.title: Greetings, pilots!
notes.notes:
The game release is coming soon, and until then, I’ll be sharing regular updates about the mechanics, features, and progress of Remote Reaper: FPV Drone.

This game is being developed by one person. I do my best to consider all your feedback and implement suggestions where possible, balancing them with development priorities.

Remote Reaper: FPV Drone is a dynamic casual simulator where you take control of combat FPV drones. Your main goal is to destroy enemy vehicles, complete combat missions, and deal with enemy defenses, including armor and electronic warfare (EW) systems.

🔹 Just like in any simulator, you can control the drone using a controller, but simple and accessible keyboard and mouse controls are also available — anyone can learn to fly.
🔹 The enemies won’t sit idle — every target is protected by air defense systems that will actively try to shoot down your drone.
🔹 One of the key features is the armored targets system. Every strike must be carefully planned; otherwise, you risk losing your drone without causing any damage.

Remote Reaper: FPV Drone is a simulator suitable for everyone who wants to feel like an FPV drone operator and experience the reality of modern drone warfare.

Stay tuned — there’s much more about game mechanics, development insights, and plans!
